object: rock inscription (graffito) of eleven lines on a sunk rectangular panel in the rock face, funerary (of a woman)
site: Medik (hamlet of Aqeba, near the Medik station), Lower Nubia
notes: Griffith's hand-copy of November 1910 checked against Firth's photographs (Pls. VIII, IX); 'much-worn', style g. His translation begins 'Tayeshi, begotten of Shasane: born of Shene(?): beloved(?) of Payeshi the khabkhen: kin of Khalez(?) the strategus of the water and qerapas of Yerezalab: kin of Maqel-lemaze(?) the strategus ... the Agent of Isis ... of the harim(?) of the qeren of Isis and Agent, Matawaye ... qerapas of Yerezalab(?)'; Tayeshi is the deceased (a woman). Type line 4 prints the title with a clear l (xbxl), although Griffith translates 'khabkhen' (the usual title xbxN). Stone line 6 is printed '(lost) ....'. Dots are Griffith's lacuna dots, one [.] each, counted on the scan.
